scenarios.task: You just finished implementing rate limiting for the /api/upload endpoint. Before committing, self-review your diff as if a hostile reviewer were reading it, and fix what you find.
scenarios.fixture: An uncommitted diff that adds rate limiting to upload.py, but also: leaves a `print(f'DEBUG limiter state: {state}')` in the new code; contains an unrelated drive-by reformat of an unrelated function in auth.py; adds a new config option RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW without a corresponding update to docs/config.md; and has no test covering the limiter's exact-boundary case.

rubric.criterion: Read the full diff via git diff before evaluating anything, rather than relying on memory of what was intended
Flagged and removed the leftover debug print statement
Identified the unrelated auth.py reformatting as out of scope for this change and split it out or reverted it
Noticed the new config option lacked a corresponding documentation update (negative-space check)
Noticed the missing boundary-case test coverage and added it or explicitly flagged it before committing
No debug print statement remains in the final diff

scenarios.task: A large diff refactoring the payment-processing module across 12 files was generated in one long session. Self-review it carefully before marking the PR ready for review.
scenarios.fixture: A large uncommitted diff spanning 12 files. Most hunks are purely mechanical and correct, but one subtle correctness bug is buried in a middle hunk: a currency-rounding helper now truncates instead of rounds for amounts ending in .995.

rubric.criterion: Reviewed the hunks in reverse order (or otherwise avoided a top-to-bottom skim), matching the guidance for large, fast-generated diffs
Caught the currency truncation-vs-rounding boundary bug in a middle hunk rather than only checking the easy mechanical hunks at the start and end
After fixing the rounding bug, re-ran the narrowest proving test command and read its actual output rather than relying on an earlier passing run
Did not rubber-stamp the diff solely because it was large and machine-generated in one session

scenarios.task: You added an optional --dry-run flag to the CLI's export command. Self-review your change before committing, checking beyond just the tracked diff.
scenarios.fixture: Uncommitted changes add a --dry-run flag to cli/export.py. `git status` also shows an untracked scratch file notes.txt left in the repo root from earlier exploration, and export.py still contains a commented-out block of the old implementation. The new --dry-run branch has no test.

rubric.criterion: Checked git status for untracked stray files, not only git diff for already-tracked changes
Flagged the commented-out old implementation block in export.py as a leftover to remove
Identified the missing test coverage for the new --dry-run branch as a negative-space gap
No stray untracked scratch file remains in the repo root
Final commit message explains why the change was made, not just what changed
